2. In Writ Petition No.17056 of 2012, Rule Nisi has been issued calling upon the respondents to show cause as to why the impugned Memos, bearing No. BR Dhaka No. 98/98/792 dated 1-10-2012 and No. BR Dhaka 98/98/799 dated 2-10-2012, Annexures-1 and 1(1) respectively, both issued under the signature of Respondent No. 4 requesting Respondents No. 5 to 7 not to register any type of transfer/sale deed covering the properties in CS Plot No. 2497 and 2582 of CS Khatian No. 118 Mouza Baunia, JL No. 211 as found at page 510 of the "projabily property" Gazette (Annexure-C) which corresponds to SA Khatian Nos. 118/41, 118/76, 183, 184, 188, 198, 212, 220, 174, 179, 118/2 and 234 and also corresponds to RS Plot Nos. 6108, 6109, 6110, 6112 and 6116 of RS Khatian Nos. 63, 116, 117, 181, 240, 811, 818, 819, 862, 1083, 1371, 1490 and 1589, should not be declared to have been issued without lawful authority and of no legal effect, and/or pass such other or further order or, orders to this Court may seem fit and proper. 

 3. Similarly, in Writ Petition No.17216 of 2012, Rule Nisi has been issued calling upon the respondents to show cause as to why the impugned Memos, bearing No. BR Dhaka No. 98/98/792 dated 1-10-2012 and No. BR-Dhaka/98/98 / 799 dated 2-10-2012, Annexures J and J(1) respectively, both issued under the signature of Respondent No. 4 requesting Respondent Nos. 5 to 7 not to register any type of or further order or orders as to this Court may seem fit and proper. 

 4. Facts necessary for the disposal of Rule in Writ Petition No. 17056 of 2012, in short, are that the writ petitioners being involved in purchase and selling lands upon developing the same, intended to purchase 5.16 acre land of CS plot No. 2497 and 9.72 acre land of CS plot No. 2582, both of CS khatian No.118 of Mouza Baunia, under Police Station Pallabi, District-Dhaka, and accordingly contacted Md Ahsanullah and others, the SA, RS and Dhaka City Survey recorded owners, who are owning and possessing the same upon paying the land Development Taxes, in their names, to the government regularly. The said Writ petitioners, after being satisfied with the right, title and possession of the said owners in the aforesaid government records, took 9 registered powers of Attorney in their favour from the aforesaid owners in possession. But when the writ petitioners went to the respondent No. 6, the concerned sub-Registrar of Mirpur, for execution and registration of the deeds of sale by using those powers the said respondent refused to register the same on the plea that by the aforesaid two impugned Memoranda, being No. BR Dhaka-98/98/792, dated 1-10-212 and BR Dhaka-98/98/799 dated 2-10-2012 issued under the signature of respondent No.4, the present Manager, Court of Wards, Bhawal Raj Estate, under the management of the land Reform Board (Respondent No.3), he has been directed not to register any deed of transfer in respect of the said plots mentioned in the said two impugned memoranda. 

 5. On the other hand, the facts of the writ petition No. 17216 of 2012, in short, are that the writ petitioners, being a developer Company and its Managing Director, respectively, earlier purchased the properties contained in 17 CS Plots of Baunia Mouza, under Police Station Pallabi, from its lawful owners in possession, whose names have been duly successively recorded in the SA, RS and Dhaka City Survey khatians. Out of the aforesaid 17 CS plot 12 CS(plots being No. 2035, 2106, 2137, 2142, 2151, 2176, 2972, 2976, 2977, 2987, 3280, 3290 and 2977/3459, were commonly recorded under three CS Khatians being No. 554, 555 and 556 amongst which, two CS khatians, namely, 554 and 555 comprising of plot numbers 13, 285, 212, 3280, 2035, 2106, 3290, 2116, 3295, 2137, 2142, 2150, 2151, 2176, 2972, 2976, 2977, 2987, 3001, 3030, and 2977/3457 are recorded in the name of two private persons in the cadastral survey (CS) Khatian, who have had no connection, whatsoever, with the Court of Wards, Annexures B and B(1), respectively. The other CS khatian, being No. 556, was recorded in the name of the original owner, the then Zamindar, represented by the Court of Wards(Annexure-B-2). The remaining four CS plots, being No. 2748 and 2970 under CS khatian No. 118 and CS plot No. 3279 and No. 3280/3438 under CS khatian No. 12 and 646 respectively, were also recorded in the name of the original owner, the then Zamindar, represented by the Court of Wards in the CS record Annexure-C, C(1) and C(2) respectively, which were settled with the "projas" and, as such the said lands covering the aforesaid four khatians being "Projabily properties" the rent receiving interests thereof were acquired by the then government under the then government under the State Acquisition and Tenancy Act, 1950, by way of publishing "projabily property" gazette (Annexure-D) for which the rent received i.e. the Zamindar received compensations, as evident from Annexure-D(1). Pursuant to Annexure D and D (1) the Zamindars, as well as the Court of Wards, lost all right, title, interest and possession in those properties/plots by operation of section 3 of the State Acquisition and Tenancy Act, 1950. Consequently, all the subsequent record of rights, namely, the SA, RS and Dhaka City Survey. were duly prepared and finally published in the names of the previous projas upgrading them as owners and their subsequent successors and transferees as "owners' in possession whose title and possession are protected against all, under the State Acquisition and Tenancy Act, 1950 as well as by the subsequent enactment of President's Order (PO) 90 of 1972. Under such circumstances, the writ petitioners, having purchased the said properties from the SA, RS and Dhaka City Survey recorded owners, went to respondent No. 6 for registration of the deeds of transfer of their purchased properties from those khatians to the subsequent transferees as well as also for registration of the deeds of purchase of other properties from the said plots but the said respondent, pursuant to the aforesaid two impugned Memoranda No. BR Dhaka-98/98/ 792, dated 1-10-2012 and BR Dhaka-98/98/799 dated 2-10-2012, Annexure-J and J(1), respectively, declined to register any transfer deed on the plea that respondent No. 4, Manager, Court of Wards, prohibited him from registering any deed connecting the aforesaid CS plots. 

 6. Further case of the writ petitioners of both the writ petitions are that the aforesaid two impugned memos are illegal and are of no legal effect as Respondent No. 3, the Manager Court of Wards, has no right, title, possession or authority to issue such, impugned Memos after publication of the "projabily property" Gazette (Annexure-C and D in the aforesaid two writ petitions respectively) after the State Acquisition and Tenancy Act, 1950 came into operation and also that the Respondent No. 3 and 4 are neither the controlling authority of the respondent Nos. 5 to 7 nor those-respondents are answerable to respondent Nos.3 and 4. Moreover, President's Order No. 90 of 1972 has imposed a complete bar in claiming ownership over the "projabily properties" by the previous Zamindars or any one claiming through the said Zamindars. Hence these two Rules. 

 7. The Respondents Nos. 3 and 4 namely, the Land Reforms Board and the Court of Wards, entered appearance in both the Rules and filed affidavits in opposition contending inter alia that on the basis of recent decision and the directive of the Ministry of Land and also the Parliamentary Standing Committee for Ministry of Land, registration of any deed of transfer of any property belonging to the then Bhawal Raj Estate which are managed by the Court of Wards, has been stopped for the purpose of preserving the historic and heritage properties of the Bhawal Raj as such the said respondents have issued the impugned memos being duty bound to protect the interest of the Bhawal Raj. The said respondents in their affidavits did not deny the facts of acquisition of the rent receiving interest by the government. Rather in para 3 they also admitted the facts stated in the writ petitions stating to be matters of record. However, in para 10 they stated that the last record of right i.e. ''Dhaka City Survey;" was erroneously prepared and published in the name of illegal occupiers, which they did not establish by any paper. Having gone through the said affidavit-in-opposition, we could not understand the head and tail of the same. The affidavits in opposition filed in Writ Petition No.17056 of 2012 is not only chaotic but also Confusing. The respondents did not state as to how the property belongs to the court of wards or how the same are not "Projabily Properties" or how Annexure C and D to the aforesaid two writ petitions respectively, do not focus on the correct picture nor they could show that the court of wards took appropriate steps in last 60 years to protect the properties of the Bhawal Raj. Similar is the position in respect of the affidavit-in-opposition filed in Writ Petition No. 17216 of 2012. 

 12. Heard the learned Advocates of both the parties, perused the two writ petitions, the affidavits in opposition and the Annexures appended to the two writ petitions. It appears that the properties of writ petition No. 17056 of 2012 bearing CS plot No. 2497 and 2582 have been recorded in CS Khatian No. 118 along with other CS plots. The said CS khatian No.118 appears at page 510 of the "projabily property" Gazette dated 24-3-1952 (Annexure-C) by which the rent receiving interest of the then Zamindars have been acquired by the government under section 3 of the State Acquisition and Tenancy Act, 1950. It also appears that the previous Zamindar Kumar Rabindra Narayan Roy Chowdhury has been paid up compensation for that purpose, as evident from compensation payment Gazette Notification No. 3126 dated 27-2-1956 published on 29-2-1956 in the then Dhaka Gazette, Annexure-C(1), by the then Government. Similarly, the properties of the writ petition No. 17216 of 2012, as it appears from Annexure B, B(1), B(2) and Annexures C, C (1) and C(2), that 43 CS plots in 6 Khatians out of which plots No. 2035, 2106, 2137, 2142, 2977, 2151, 2176, 2972, 2976, 2977, 2987, 3280, 3290 and 2977/3459 of CS Khatian 554 as well as those total khatian No. 555, total 26 plots, have been recorded in the names of private individuals, not the Zamindar or the court of wards. As such the court of wards has no connection, whatsoever, with the same. On the other hand 13 plots bearing same numbers namely, 2035, 2106, 2137, 2142, 2151, 2176, 2972, 2976, 2977, 2987, 3280, 3290 and 2977/3459 of CS Khatian No. 556 along with CS plots No.2748 and 2970 of CS khatian No.118 CS plot No.3280/3438 of CS Khatian No. 646 and CS plot No. 3279 of CS khatian No. 12 (total 17 plots) all were originally recorded in the name of the then Zamindar, Kumar Rabindra Narayan Ray Chowdhury, represented by the Court of Wards, the respondent No. 4, in the CS Survey, as appears from Annexure B, B(1), B(2), C,C(1) and C(2) respectively, which were settled with the. "projas" as underraiyts. Thereafter, with the enactment of the Statement Acquisition and Tenancy Act, 1950 the rent receiving interest the raiyots i.e. the then Zamindars vested with the government and the "projas" were upgraded and recognized by the government as owners of their settled land they had been possessing under the Zamindar. Under such circumstances in all subsequent surveys the previous "projas" and their successors names have been recorded as owners, duly recognized by the government. But it reveals that all the plots mentioned above in six khatians which have been recorded in the names of the then projas or their successors have been claimed as the properties of the Court of Wards without providing any khatian number by the impugned memos. On Examination of the "projabily property" Gazette it appears that the plots of CS khatian No. 556, 118, 646 and khatian No. 12 have been duly recorded as "projabily properties" whose "rent receiving" interests of the then Zamindars have been acquired by the government under the State Acquisition and Tenancy Act 1950. As such whatever rights, title and interest, the Court of Wards, if any, had, in all these plots, have been ceased by the Government. In Annexure C to writ petition No. 17056 of 2012, the "Projabily Property" Gazette, at page 510 plots of CS khatian No. 118 have been enlisted as projabili properties. Similarly in Annexure-D to the writ petition No. 17216 of 2012 all the plots of CS khatians No.12, 118, 556 and 646 have been shown at pages 503, 510 and at page 516 respectively in the "projabily property" Gazette. 

 13. It further appears that following the "projabily property" Gazette the SA khatianswere published recording the names of the then "projas" upon upgrading their status as the "owners" in different SA khatians by the Survey and Settlement Department of the Government. Similarly, the next RS khatians were also prepared and published recording the names of the said "projas"/"owners" and their subsequent legal heirs and assignees as "owners". The Land Reform Board and the Court of wards as respondent No. 3 and 4, in both the writ petitions, respectively, did not deny the statements in respect of publishing the "projabily property" Gazette and the compensation payment Gazette and preparation and final publication of the SA and RS record of rights in the names of the previous "projas" and their successors in interests as "owners". Even in respect of preparation and publication of the recent Dhaka City Survey record the respondents frankly admitted, in paragraph-10 of their affidavit that those were recorded in the name of the previous "projas" as "owners" but claimed that those recordings as wrong although no step has yet been taken by the respondents to correct the said final recording, of course time allowed for correction of such wrong recording, as alleged, has expired long before. The learned Advocate for the petitioners referring to the "projabily property" Gazette (Annexure-C and D in the aforesaid two writ petitions, respectively) and also to the PO 90 of 1972 (Annexure-D and E in the aforesaid two writ petitions, respectively) and also to the decision of the Appellate Division in the case reported in 33 DLR (AD) /3 and 53, 27 DLR (SC) 109, and14 MLR (AD) 401 submitted that the Appellate Division in those cases has, already settled that the property mentioned in the "projabily property" Gazette are the properties of the projas and their successors in interests, as the rent receiving interest, therein, of the previous Zamindars have been acquired by the Government. As such when the petitioners went for registering the transfer deeds of the land purchased from the successor in interest of the then "projas", whose names 'have been correctly recorded and finally published in the aforesaid Khatians, the respondents No. 5 to 7' have no authority to refuse registration on the direction of respondents No. 3 and 4. Thus haying not done what they are suppose to do under the law they have committed illegality in not registering the deeds. 

 14. Under such circumstances, when the said plots are published, in the gazette notification as "Projabily Properties" and the rent receiving interests of the then Zamindars are acquired under section 3 of the State Acquisition and Tenancy Act 1950 (hereafter referred to as the SAT Act) the same no longer belongs to the then Zamindars or the Court of Wards rather to the "projas" as per SAT Act 1950 who have been upgraded and declared to be the "owners", the respondents have no authority to issue the impugned notices. Moreover when no khatian number has been mentioned, in the impugned memos simply mentioning the CS plot, numbers does not specify the land as such, the impugned notices are vague and indefinite by which no legal force can be ascertained. Section 3 of the State Acquisition and Tenancy Act, 1950, reads as follows: 

 (ii) All interests of all rent-receivers whose properties are, the court of Wards Act, 1879, in their respective estates, (taluks, tenures, holdings ortenancies), as the case may be including all their interests in all sub-soil and rights to minerals in such estates, (taluks, tenures, holdings or tenancies) 

 "2. Notwithstanding anything contained in any other law for the time being in force, on the commencement of this order, all suits, appeals, application and other legal proceedings pending or, continuing or deemed to be pending or continuing in any court against the Government of the People's Republic of Bangladesh in which the legality or validity of the State and Tenancy Act, 1950 (EB Act No. XXVIII of 1950), or of the East Bengal State Acquisition and Tenancy (Amendment) Ordinance, 1956 (EB Ordinance No III of 1956), or of any other law making any amendment in the said Act, or of the acquisition of any property made under any provision thereof is challenged or called in question shall abate, and all orders, including orders of injunction and other interlocutory orders, passed in such suits, appeals, applications and other legal proceedings shall cease to have any effect; and no court shall entertain, and no person shall bring, any fresh suit, appeal, application or other legal proceedings in which the legality or validity of any such law or acquisition is challenged or called in question ." 

 16. The Appellate Division in the case of People's Republic of Bangladesh vs Sri Sri Madan Gopal Jew Bigraha , reported in 33 DLR (AD) 13 after considering and discussing the legal effect of the aforesaid laws, held that 'with the publication of notifications under section 3 all rent-receiving interests including wakf and debuttor property stood acquired by and vested in the Government'. Again in the ease of Promode Ranjan Saha and others vs Government of Bangladesh and another, reported in 33 DLR (AD) 53 it has been observed that 'after the promulgation of PO 90 of 72 all orders including orders of injunction, etc. passed in appeals, application, etc. shall cease to have any effect and no court shall entertain any fresh suit, appeal, application, etc. in which the legality of any such law of acquisition is challenged or called in question'. In the case of Anwara Begum Chowdhurani vs Nur Jahan Begum reported in 27 DLR (AD) 109 it has been held that 'after the notification issued under section 3 of the Act the status of the under-raiyat became upgraded to that of raiyat. The rent receiving interests can be acquired even before the preparation of record of rights and publication of compensation assessment rolls'. It has further been held therein that 'with the acquisition of the rent-receiving interests by the government all intermediary interests disappeared and a person holding the land under the government becomes a "tenant", becomes a "raiyat" or a "Malik" of the land recognized by the government. Consequently, the under-raiyat who actually holds the land becomes a tenant under the government. Superior land lord (i.e. the raiyat) of an under-raiyat by virtue of elimination of his rent-receiving interests disappears and the under-raiyat is upgraded to the status of a "raiyat". Lastly, in the case of Bhawal Raj Court of Wards Estate vs Rasheda Begum and others reported in 14 MLR (AD) 401 the Appellate Division has held " record of rights prepared and finally published under section 144 cannot be varied by any authority and remedy of wrong entry if any lies with the appropriate court'. It has further been held in that judgment by the Appellate Division that "Manager, Bhawal Raj estate, Court of Wards can manage only the retainable land." The Appellate Division in the aforesaid cases has already settled that the property enlisted/ shown in the "projabily property" Gazette are the properties of "projas" who have been accepted as "owners" and the "rent receiving" interest whatsoever it had therein, of the Zamindars all vested to the Government by operation of SAT Act, 1950. The relevant portion of the finding of the Appellate Division in the case reported in 14 MLR (AD) 401 are as follows: 

 "The learned advocate appearing for the leave petitioner, when confronted with the aforesaid gazette notifications dated 24-3-1952 and 29-2-956, as to acquisition of rent receiving interest and the vesting of lands of the leave petitioners, including the case lands, found it difficult to substantiate the locus-standi of the leave petitioner in challenging the draft records of right prepared in the names of the respective writ petitioners in respect of their respective case lands prepared during the Mohanagar Survey. Further with the publication of the gazette notifications dated 24-3-1952 and 29-2-1956 the leave petitioner ceased to have any right, title and interest and possession in the case lands, because of acquisition, and vesting of said lands in the Government. "Thereafter, the full bench of the Hon'ble Appellate Division, on an application corrected the said judgment stating that the rent receiving interest of Projabily Property had vested to the Government and land has been vested to the projas as owners. In that case the Court of Wards, Bhawal Raj Estate and the Land Reform Board the present contesting respondents were parties and had challenged the Dhaka City Survey khatian prepared and published in the names of the successors in interests of the projas". The Apex Court in that case further held: 

 17. In the aforesaid judgment the Appellate Division lastly held that the Court of Wards can only keep in his custody, the retainable khas land of the previous Zamindars (which was 375 bighas at the time of SAT Act, 1950) and not the "projabily property". It may be mentioned, in this connection, that the land holding limitation (hereafter has been reduced to 100 bighas and lastly to 60 bighas). On the face of the aforesaid decision of the Appellate Division the Court of Wards and Land Reform Board, cannot, under any circumstances, claim ownership over the Projabily Property of the previous Zamindar, Kumar Rabindra Narayan Ray Chowdhury and, as such, cannot issue the impugned two Memoranda, specifically when they were parties in the aforesaid case before the Appellate Division. Such interference by the respondents are nothing but harassment to the previous "projas" who has become owners of their respective properties by operation of law. 

 19. Considering the provisions of law mentioned above and the findings of the Appellate Division in the aforesaid cited cases we are of the view that the property in question in both the Rules being "Projabily properties", as evident from Annexures C and D to Writ Petition No. 17056 of 2012 and Writ Petition No. 17216 of 2012, respectively, and the same being finally published in SA, RS and Dhaka Mohanagar City Survey khatians in the name of the predecessors in interest of the petitioners and the then Zamindars having not taken any step in respect of wrong entry, as claimed by the respondents, the court of wards, the said respondents cannot, under any circumstance, claim that the property belongs to the court of wards. As such when the property does not belong to the court of wards the court of wards has no legal authority to direct the registering authority not to register any deed of transfer in respect of the said properties. 

 21. Moreover, under the Registration Act and the Registration Manual the Registrar derives its powers and authorities of registering any deed as well as the same is under the control of the Ministry of Law. Whereas, the Court of Wards being under the control of the Land Reform Board is not a superior authority of the Registrars and Sub-Registrars to impose any prohibitory order in respect of registering any deed. According to section 53(A) of the Registration Act, the concerned Registrar/Sub-Registrar has been given a guideline as to which property can be registered and which property cannot be registered. So, if the Registrar/Sub-Registrars are restrained by the two impugned Memos at the instance of the Manager, Court of Wards, even if the criteria of section 53A is fulfilled, it would be an unwarranted interference by an unauthorized person in the lawful function of the registrar/sub-Registrar which is not permitted under the law. Nor the respondents have any right to issue such direction upon respondents No. 5 to 7 and the Registrar, under the law, is not obligated to abide by such illegal directions issued by unauthorized persons like respondents No. 3 and 4. 

 22. Apart from the above, we want to focus about the role of the learned advocate for the respondents as well as the respondents No. 3 and 4. We find it very difficult to understand from the affidavit-in-opposition filed by the Respondents No. 3 and 4 that what is the gist of the case of the respondents and the respondents without stating the fact that the respondents are the owners of the land and, as such, have issued such directions upon the registering authority rather stated that the impugned memos have been issued for protecting the historic and heritage properties of Bhawal Raj. Nor the respondents could show that the registering authority has responsibility to abide by such directions and thereby refusal to registration has been done in accordance with law. On the other hand, respondents No. 3 and 4 could not come forward with any piece of document to show that they have right, title or possession in the land in question, specifically, when the property has been published in the gazette notification under section 3 of the State Acquisition and Tenancy Act, 1950 and the said publication being finalized and protected by PO 90 of 1972, the respondents No. 3 and 4 did not come for-ward to assist the court by showing a piece of paper for the said plots, which have already been recorded in the name of the projas fall within the "retainable khas land" of the Zamindars being up to 375 bighas with the commencement of the SAT Act, 1950 which has subsequently been reduced to 100 Bigas and lastly to 60 bighas. The respondents No. 3 and 4 did not even come forward with any piece of paper to show that the limit of retainable khas land has been raised to more than 60 bighas for which the court of wards can act as the custodian. 

 25. Before withdrawing our pen, we would like to note that, now a days time and again we are confronted with unnecessary and uncalled for litigations like the present one in spite of settling the selfsame issue connecting with "projabily property" by the Apex court in its different decisions reported in, 33 DLR (AD) 13 and 53, 27 DLR (SC) 109 and lastly in the case reported in 14 MLR (AD) 401. In these two writ petitions the question over the title of "projabily property" of the previous Zamindar, Kumar Rabindra Narayan Roy Chowdhury, represented by the Court of Wards, Bhawal Raj Estate, again came up for our consideration as the court of Wards claimed the "projabily property" as its own property and accordingly issued the two "impugned Memoranda, though it has already been settled earlier in the aforesaid cases holding that the "projabily properly" can never be claimed by the previous Zamindars represented by the court of Wards. The Court of Wards though legally bound to follow the said decision according to Article 112 of the constitution but time and again they are harassing the people claiming title over the "projabily property", either by issuing Memorandum or by other ways and means and thereby also wasting the courts valuable time. So it is high time to caution the Court of Wards, Bhawal Raj Estate and also the Land Reform Board to abstain from creating such situation on frivolous issues and thereby pushing the public to the Court. Thus they are cautioned not to harass anybody specifically the previous "projas" or their successors-in-interests any more, claiming title over the "projabily property" as cited in the "projabily property" gazette published on 24-3-1952. If in future, any such illegal and uncalled for claim is sought for by the court of wards or if any litigation is continuing or started afresh because of court of wards action by claiming title over the said "projabily property" by the Court of Wards and the Land Reform Board, then they would be liable to be dealt with for contempt of Court, apart from such litigations been abated under PO 90 of 1972. 

 26. Under such circumstances we think it would be proper to call the manager, court of wards and the Land Administrator to explain their position in this respect because the government officials under no circumstances can play with the property of the general people. This court thus thought that exercising the power conferred under the law we should call the said officials to explain their conduct as to these two cases in particular. But considering that it will be nothing but a futile exercise of this Court on the matter, because when the respondents could not come forward with a proper affidavit giving proper explanations supported by the papers, we simply can express our anxiety and great concern that the government officials are doing this only to harass the general people of the country and thereby they are trying to have some personal gain over it As such the respondents No. 3 and 4 are cautioned not to deal with such property of the general people in such manner which can be subject matter of harassment of the general people.
